paragraphs.text: Let every soul be in subjection to the higher powers: for there is no power but of God; and the [powers] that be are ordained of God.
paragraphs.original: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτασσέσθω, οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἐξουσία εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ θεοῦ, αἱ δὲ οὖσαι ὑπὸ θεοῦ τεταγμέναι εἰσίν.
paragraphs.translit: Pasa psychē exousiais hyperechousais hypotassesthō, ou gar estin exousia ei mē hypo theou, hai de ousai hypo theou tetagmenai eisin.

paragraphs.text: Therefore he that resisteth the power, withstandeth the ordinance of God: and they that withstand shall receive to themselves judgment.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν, οἱ δὲ ἀνθεστηκότες ἑαυτοῖς κρίμα λήμψονται.
paragraphs.translit: hōste ho antitassomenos tē exousia tē tou theou diatagē anthestēken, hoi de anthestēkotes heautois krima lēmpsontai.

paragraphs.text: For rulers are not a terror to the good work, but to the evil. And wouldest thou have no fear of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise from the same:
paragraphs.original: οἱ γὰρ ἄρχοντες οὐκ εἰσὶν φόβος τῷ ἀγαθῷ ἔργῳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κακῷ. θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν; τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει, καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς·
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar archontes ouk eisin phobos tō agathō ergō alla tō kakō. theleis de mē phobeisthai tēn exousian; to agathon poiei, kai hexeis epainon ex autēs·

paragraphs.text: for he is a minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is a minister of God, an avenger for wrath to him that doeth evil.
paragraphs.original: θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν σοὶ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν. ἐὰν δὲ τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς, φοβοῦ· οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ τὴν μάχαιραν φορεῖ· θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν, ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι.
paragraphs.translit: theou gar diakonos estin soi eis to agathon. ean de to kakon poiēs, phobou· ou gar eikē tēn machairan phorei· theou gar diakonos estin, ekdikos eis orgēn tō to kakon prassonti.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore [ye] must needs be in subjection, not only because of the wrath, but also for conscience` sake.
paragraphs.original: διὸ ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι, οὐ μόνον διὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν,
paragraphs.translit: dio anankē hypotassesthai, ou monon dia tēn orgēn alla kai dia tēn syneidēsin,

paragraphs.text: For this cause ye pay tribute also; for they are ministers of God`s service, attending continually upon this very thing.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε, λειτουργοὶ γὰρ θεοῦ εἰσιν εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσκαρτεροῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto gar kai phorous teleite, leitourgoi gar theou eisin eis auto touto proskarterountes.

paragraphs.text: Render to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute [is due]; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honor to whom honor.
paragraphs.original: ἀπόδοτε πᾶσι τὰς ὀφειλάς, τῷ τὸν φόρον τὸν φόρον, τῷ τὸ τέλος τὸ τέλος, τῷ τὸν φόβον τὸν φόβον, τῷ τὴν τιμὴν τὴν τιμήν.
paragraphs.translit: apodote pasi tas opheilas, tō ton phoron ton phoron, tō to telos to telos, tō ton phobon ton phobon, tō tēn timēn tēn timēn.

paragraphs.text: Owe no man anything, save to love one another: for he that loveth his neighbor hath fulfilled the law.
paragraphs.original: Μηδενὶ μηδὲν ὀφείλετε, εἰ μὴ τὸ ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἕτερον νόμον πεπλήρωκεν.
paragraphs.translit: Mēdeni mēden opheilete, ei mē to allēlous agapan· ho gar agapōn ton heteron nomon peplērōken.

paragraphs.text: For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not covet, and if there be any other commandment, it is summed up in this word, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
paragraphs.original: τὸ γάρ· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις, καὶ εἴ τις ἑτέρα ἐντολή, ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται, ἐν τῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
paragraphs.translit: to gar· Ou moicheuseis, Ou phoneuseis, Ou klepseis, Ouk epithymēseis, kai ei tis hetera entolē, en tō logō toutō anakephalaioutai, en tō· Agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton.

paragraphs.text: Love worketh no ill to his neighbor: love therefore is the fulfilment of the law.
paragraphs.original: ἡ ἀγάπη τῷ πλησίον κακὸν οὐκ ἐργάζεται· πλήρωμα οὖν νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη.
paragraphs.translit: hē agapē tō plēsion kakon ouk ergazetai· plērōma oun nomou hē agapē.

paragraphs.text: And this, knowing the season, that already it is time for you to awake out of sleep: for now is salvation nearer to us than when we [first] believed.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδότες τὸν καιρόν, ὅτι ὥρα ἤδη ὑμᾶς ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθῆναι, νῦν γὰρ ἐγγύτερον ἡμῶν ἡ σωτηρία ἢ ὅτε ἐπιστεύσαμεν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai touto eidotes ton kairon, hoti hōra ēdē hymas ex hypnou egerthēnai, nyn gar engyteron hēmōn hē sōtēria ē hote episteusamen.

paragraphs.text: The night is far spent, and the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light.
paragraphs.original: ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν, ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤγγικεν. ἀποβαλώμεθα οὖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ σκότους, ἐνδυσώμεθα δὲ τὰ ὅπλα τοῦ φωτός.
paragraphs.translit: hē nyx proekopsen, hē de hēmera ēngiken. apobalōmetha oun ta erga tou skotous, endysōmetha de ta hopla tou phōtos.

paragraphs.text: Let us walk becomingly, as in the day; not in revelling and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and jealousy.
paragraphs.original: ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν, μὴ κώμοις καὶ μέθαις, μὴ κοίταις καὶ ἀσελγείαις, μὴ ἔριδι καὶ ζήλῳ,
paragraphs.translit: hōs en hēmera euschēmonōs peripatēsōmen, mē kōmois kai methais, mē koitais kai aselgeiais, mē eridi kai zēlō,

paragraphs.text: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to [fulfil] the lusts [thereof].
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, καὶ τῆς σαρκὸς πρόνοιαν μὴ ποιεῖσθε εἰς ἐπιθυμίας.
paragraphs.translit: alla endysasthe ton kyrion Iēsoun Christon, kai tēs sarkos pronoian mē poieisthe eis epithymias.
